experiments.why: A typical V3 channel frame with snr 12.5 and an rssi byte of -90 at offset 2, which the new decoder adds beside the existing fields.
An exactly 11-byte header-only channel frame whose formerly reserved byte 2 is zero, so the new code reports rssi 0 for a frame that carries none.
A 10-byte channel frame one byte short of the header, which must still return null without throwing.
A plain V3 contact frame with snr -1 and rssi -80, checking the existing fields while rssi is newly read from offset 2.
A SIGNED_PLAIN contact frame, checking that reading rssi leaves the 4-byte sender prefix and the body offset at 20 alone.
An exactly 16-byte header-only contact frame with 0x80 at offset 2, the signed-byte boundary that must decode as rssi -128.

source.quote: decodes snr/4, channel idx, timestamp, and splits the "name: " prefix

obligations.statement: For a V3 channel frame (0x11, path_len at offset 5, txt_type at 6, uint32 LE timestamp at 7, body from 11), decodeChannelMsgV3 keeps returning snrDb as the signed byte at offset 1 divided by 4 (12.5 in the test), the channel index, pathLen, timestampUnix, and a cleanBody with the "name: " prefix spl
decodeChannelMsgV3 returns null, without throwing, for any frame shorter than 11 bytes.

source.quote: accepts an 11-byte frame (header-only, empty body) as a valid empty-body message

obligations.statement: decodeChannelMsgV3 decodes an exactly 11-byte, header-only frame as a non-null message with body '' and the header's channelIdx and timestampUnix.

source.quote: reads the 6-byte sender prefix and body (no name prefix)

obligations.statement: For a V3 contact frame (0x10, sender prefix at offsets 4..9, path_len at 10, txt_type at 11, uint32 LE timestamp at 12, body from 16), decodeContactMsgV3 keeps returning snrDb as the signed byte at offset 1 divided by 4 (-1 in the test), senderPubKeyPrefixHex from offsets 4..9, timestampUnix, and th

source.quote: strips the 4-byte sender_prefix from the body and exposes it as senderPrefixExtraHex (V3)

obligations.statement: For a V3 contact frame with txt_type SIGNED_PLAIN (2), decodeContactMsgV3 returns txtType SIGNED_PLAIN, the 4 bytes at offsets 16..19 as senderPrefixExtraHex, and only the text from offset 20 as body, with no sender-prefix bytes in it.

source.quote: reports snrDb 0 and reads the older layout

obligations.statement: For a legacy 0x08 channel frame (channel index at offset 1, path_len at 2, txt_type at 3, uint32 LE timestamp at 4, body from 8), decodeChannelMsgV1 returns snrDb 0 together with that channelIdx, timestampUnix and body.

source.quote: reads the 6-byte sender prefix and body, snrDb 0

obligations.statement: For a legacy 0x07 contact frame (sender prefix at offsets 1..6, path_len at 7, txt_type at 8, uint32 LE timestamp at 9, body from 13), decodeContactMsgV1 returns snrDb 0 together with that senderPubKeyPrefixHex, pathLen, timestampUnix and body.

Given explicit flags and timestampUnix, encodeSendChannelText returns [0x03][flags][channel index][timestamp uint32 LE][UTF-8 text], e.g. hex 030002010000006869 for channelIdx 2, text 'hi', timestampUnix 1, flags 0.

source.quote: lays out [cmd][txt_type][attempt][ts u32 LE][6B pubkey prefix][text]

obligations.statement: Given an explicit timestampUnix, encodeSendDmText returns [0x02][txt_type][attempt][timestamp uint32 LE][first 6 bytes of the destination public key][UTF-8 text], so the text starts at offset 13.

source.quote: rejects a public key shorter than 6 bytes

obligations.statement: encodeSendDmText throws an error matching /≥6 bytes/ when destPublicKeyHex is shorter than 6 bytes, such as 'aabb'.

source.quote: decodeSentAck reads flood flag, expected ack, and est timeout

obligations.statement: For a 10-byte 0x06 frame, decodeSentAck returns flood true when byte 1 is 1, expectedAckHex from bytes 2..5, and estTimeoutMs from the uint32 LE at offset 6.

source.quote: decodeSendConfirmed reads ack hash and trip time

obligations.statement: For a 9-byte 0x82 frame, decodeSendConfirmed returns ackHex from bytes 1..4 and tripTimeMs from the uint32 LE at offset 5.
